name: GitHub
about: repos, Actions, issues and pull requests
benefit: With this token, your agent can open pull requests, triage issues and run GitHub Actions on the repositories you select.

key.name: GH_TOKEN
key.label: Access token
steps: Choose the **Resource owner** and repositories.
Review the prefilled permissions and expiration.
Select **Generate token** and copy it.
key.note: The form preselects writes for code, workflows, secrets and repo admin.

access: The prefilled token requests repository writes, including administration, workflows and secrets. Pick one owner and choose all or selected repositories. You can adjust permissions and expiration before creating it. Organization policy may require approval.
verify: Run godmode run GH_TOKEN -- gh api user --jq .login to check the identity. Then read a repository under the selected owner. Each write needs its own endpoint permissions.
recover: Check the owner, repository selection and approval status. Replace a revoked or expired token with godmode set GH_TOKEN.

docs.title: Start with a blank fine-grained token form

name: Cloudflare
about: Workers, D1, R2, DNS and email
benefit: Cloudflare hosts websites and runs serverless functions. Your agent can deploy a Worker in your account or update DNS for a domain you select.

key.name: CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN
key.label: API token
steps: Select **Create Token**. Choose **Edit Zone DNS** or **Edit Cloudflare Workers**.
Select your DNS zone or Workers account. Review any route permissions.
Review the summary, select **Create Token** and copy it.

access: DNS changes need DNS Edit on the intended zone. Worker code needs Workers Scripts Edit on the account. Custom routes also need Workers Routes Edit on the zone. Add D1 or R2 permissions for those services. For broad access, start with Read All Resources and change the services you need to Edit. R2’s S3 interface uses separate credentials. Domain registration needs Registrar write access, billing, a default registrant contact and acceptance of the registration agreement.
verify: Check the token at GET /client/v4/user/tokens/verify, then list the intended Worker, database or DNS zone. For unattended Wrangler commands, set CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID to select the account. Before buying a domain, confirm availability, price and authorization.
recover: Edit the resource selection or permissions in API Tokens. For a lost value, create a replacement and save it with godmode set CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN. Rolling the original immediately invalidates it.

docs.title: Registrar API beta prerequisites and workflow
Registrar API support and billing requirements

name: Vercel
benefit: A Vercel token lets your agent deploy a web app, inspect a preview and connect a domain to your project.

key.name: VERCEL_TOKEN
key.label: Access token
steps: Make a token for your project, team or **Full Account**.
Name it, choose an expiration, select **Create** and copy it.

access: Full Account covers your personal account and teams within your role. Team scope covers all projects on a team, and project scope covers one project. Some teams require SSO or two-factor authentication.
verify: List deployments with the Vercel CLI and VERCEL_TOKEN. To target an unlinked project in CI, set VERCEL_ORG_ID and VERCEL_PROJECT_ID together. For REST requests, use Bearer authentication and supply the team ID or slug when a full-account token targets a team.
recover: Check the team, project and expiration. For a lost or invalid token, create a new one in Account Tokens and save it with godmode set VERCEL_TOKEN.

docs.title: Access token scope, use and recovery

name: Supabase
benefit: A Supabase token lets your agent inspect hosted Postgres projects and manage Auth settings or deploy Edge Functions with the permissions you grant.

key.name: SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN
key.label: Access token
steps: Select **Generate new token** and name it.
Choose a project and permissions, or a legacy token for full access.
Set an expiration, generate the token and copy it.

access: A scoped personal token grants selected management permissions within your account role. A legacy full-access token covers every organization and project you can access, including future ones. Direct database connections need database credentials.
verify: Read the intended project with Project Settings Read using the Management API. The Supabase CLI reads SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN. Check the project reference before changing settings or deploying a function.
recover: Check your role, selected project, permissions and expiration. Generate a replacement and save it with godmode set SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN.

name: Stripe
about: payments, in test and live mode
benefit: Stripe handles checkout and payments. A secret key lets your agent test a payment flow in a sandbox or work with real payments in live mode.

key.name: STRIPE_TEST_SECRET_KEY
key.label: Test secret key
key.goal: Copy your Stripe test secret key
key.note: Use the account picker to select the sandbox you want to test.
steps: In your sandbox, open **Standard keys** and reveal the **Secret key**.
Copy the value starting with sk_test_.

key.name: STRIPE_TEST_PUBLISHABLE_KEY
key.label: Test publishable key
key.goal: Copy your Stripe test publishable key
steps: In the same sandbox, copy the **Publishable key** starting with pk_test_.

key.name: STRIPE_LIVE_SECRET_KEY
key.label: Live secret key
key.goal: Create a Stripe live secret key
steps: In live mode, select **Create secret key** and verify your identity.
Name the key and select **Create**. Copy the sk_live_ value now.
key.note: Requests with this secret can move real money.

key.name: STRIPE_LIVE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY
key.label: Live publishable key
key.goal: Copy your Stripe live publishable key
key.note: Use the live account that issued your live secret key.
steps: In live mode, copy the **Publishable key** starting with pk_live_.

access: One test or live server key is enough for its mode. A standard secret key grants full account API access in that mode. A restricted key (rk_test_ or rk_live_) limits operations by resource. Publishable keys are optional for server-side work and are used by client integrations. Each webhook endpoint has a separate signing secret.
verify: Pass the matching server key to your tool. For example, with Stripe CLI installed, run godmode run STRIPE_API_KEY=STRIPE_TEST_SECRET_KEY -- stripe balance retrieve. This checks balance access in that sandbox. For a restricted key, read a resource its permissions cover.
recover: Confirm the account, sandbox or live mode, and key permissions. Rotate a compromised or lost secret in Stripe, then replace its matching Godmode entry. Stripe lets you choose when to expire the old key.

name: PostHog
benefit: A personal PostHog key lets your agent query product usage, inspect funnels and manage feature flags within its scopes.

key.name: POSTHOG_PERSONAL_API_KEY
key.label: Personal API key
steps: Sign in to your project’s region and open **Personal API keys**.
Name the key and review its project access and scopes.
Select **Create key** and copy the personal key.

access: Use the US, EU or self-hosted instance that holds your project. Personal API keys use the selected permissions and your user access. Frontend event capture uses a separate project token.
verify: Find the project ID in project settings. Private requests go to us.posthog.com, eu.posthog.com or your self-hosted domain. With query read access, run a query at /api/projects/<project_id>/query for that project.
recover: Check the instance, project and key scopes. Replace a revoked key with godmode set POSTHOG_PERSONAL_API_KEY. Rolling a legacy key immediately invalidates its old value.

name: Notion
benefit: A Notion token lets your agent find project notes, update pages and add database entries in a workspace you choose.

key.name: NOTION_API_KEY
key.label: Access token
steps: Select **New token** and name it.
Choose the workspace, **Notion API** capability and expiration.
Select **Create token** and copy it now.

access: A personal token acts as you in one workspace. Its Notion API capability covers content you can access. Workspace policy controls who can create tokens. Internal connections use a separate identity and explicitly shared pages.
verify: Read the token identity with GET /v1/users/me, then retrieve a known page. If your script uses the official JavaScript SDK example, pass NOTION_TOKEN=NOTION_API_KEY to godmode run. The script supplies that variable as the SDK client’s auth option.
recover: Check workspace policy and your page access. Before the personal token expires, create a replacement and save it with godmode set NOTION_API_KEY. For an internal connection, check page sharing.

docs.title: Find personal access tokens in the Notion sidebar

name: Gmail
about: an inbox agents read and send from
benefit: With a mailbox address and app password, your agent can read Gmail over IMAP and send mail over SMTP.

key.name: GMAIL_USER
key.label: Mailbox address
key.goal: Type the Gmail address agents will use
steps: Enter the full address of the mailbox your agent will use.

key.name: GMAIL_APP_PASSWORD
key.label: App password
steps: Sign in as that mailbox with **2-Step Verification** enabled.
Enter an **App name**, select **Create**, then copy the 16-character password.

access: Both values belong to the same Google account. App passwords require 2-Step Verification. Advanced Protection, security-key-only sign-in or organization policy may make the option unavailable. The Gmail API uses separate OAuth authorization.
verify: Use GMAIL_USER and GMAIL_APP_PASSWORD in a mail client and authenticate over TLS to IMAP or SMTP. A successful login checks the mailbox without sending mail.
recover: Google revokes app passwords when you change the account password. Create a replacement and save it with godmode set GMAIL_APP_PASSWORD. If policy disables app passwords, use a mail client that supports Google sign-in.

name: Google
about: Ads keyword research and Search Console
benefit: Google service accounts let your agent research keywords in Ads or see which searches bring visitors to a Search Console property.

key.name: GOOGLE_ADS_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON
key.label: Ads service account
key.goal: Save a Google Ads service account key
key.prompt: Drag or paste the key file
key.note: Keyword planning needs Basic or Standard API access.
steps: Enable the Google Ads API in your project. Open a service account.
Under **Keys**, use **Add key** > **Create new key** > **JSON** and download it.
Add its email in Google Ads under **Admin** > **Access and security**.

key.name: GOOGLE_SEARCH_CONSOLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON
key.label: Search Console account
key.goal: Save a Search Console service account key
key.prompt: Drag or paste the key file
key.note: A property owner can grant access in Search Console.
steps: Enable the Search Console API in your project. Open a service account.
Under **Keys**, use **Add key** > **Create new key** > **JSON** and download it.
Add its email to the property under **Settings** > **Users and permissions**.

access: Choose either service or add both. For Ads, enable the API and grant the service-account email access to the customer or manager. Production reporting needs production access. For keyword planning, use Basic access or Standard access that permits planning. For Search Console, enable its API and grant the service-account email access to the property.
verify: Read the saved JSON into the Google client library as service-account credentials. The named variables contain JSON. GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS expects a file path.

For Ads, request the adwords scope and list accessible customers. When acting through a manager, set login-customer-id to that manager’s ID without hyphens and target the client’s ID. For Search Console reports, use webmasters.readonly and list sites to confirm the property.
recover: Access tokens refresh through the Google library. If the underlying key is disabled, create a replacement on the same service account, save it to the matching Godmode entry, verify access and retire the old key.
For user OAuth, use a separate entry for the refresh grant. Save a rotated grant explicitly or keep it in the consuming tool’s own login cache.

name: Higgsfield
benefit: A Higgsfield key lets your agent generate images and video clips with models available to your account.

key.name: HIGGSFIELD_API_KEY_ID
key.label: API key ID
key.note: The copied ID:secret pair supplies both fields. Paste it here first.
steps: In the intended account, create and name an **API key**.
Copy the full key and keep it for the next field.

key.name: HIGGSFIELD_API_KEY_SECRET
key.label: API key secret
key.goal: Paste the same Higgsfield API key again
key.note: If the original is lost, create a new pair and replace both fields.
steps: Paste the same complete pair to save its secret.

access: The ID and secret form one credential. The personal or organization account that issued it pays for generation. Organization admins manage keys. Model availability and API balance depend on the account.
verify: For the Python higgsfield-client SDK, map HF_API_KEY=HIGGSFIELD_API_KEY_ID and HF_API_SECRET=HIGGSFIELD_API_KEY_SECRET in godmode run. Call higgsfield_client.status(request_id) with an existing request. Starting a generation can incur charges.
recover: Check expiration, account and model availability. For a disabled or lost key, create one replacement and update both Godmode entries from that pair.

docs.title: Python SDK credential names and status method

name: Zernio
benefit: A Zernio key lets your agent schedule posts and check publishing status for social accounts you connect.

key.name: ZERNIO_API_KEY
key.label: API key
steps: Select **Create API key** and name it.
Choose the profiles and permissions, create the key and copy it.
key.note: Connect a social account to a Zernio profile before publishing.

access: The key’s resource and profile scopes control access to Zernio. To publish, connect a social account to the intended profile and approve the platform permissions.
verify: Use the SDK with ZERNIO_API_KEY to list profiles and connected accounts. Check the intended account ID and connection status before scheduling a post.
recover: Replace an expired or revoked API key with godmode set ZERNIO_API_KEY. If a single platform disconnects, reauthorize that social account in Zernio.

docs.title: Create an API key and connect social accounts

name: Prodigi
benefit: A Prodigi key lets your agent quote print jobs, test orders in a sandbox or submit live orders for printing and shipping.

key.name: PRODIGI_SANDBOX_API_KEY
key.label: Sandbox API key
key.goal: Copy your Prodigi sandbox API key
key.note: pwinty.com is Prodigi’s sandbox dashboard. Sign in with Prodigi.
steps: In sandbox **Settings** > **Integrations** > **API**, select **Show API Key**.
Copy the key as shown. Your client adds sandbox_ for v5.

key.name: PRODIGI_API_KEY
key.label: Live API key
key.goal: Copy your Prodigi live API key
key.note: Submitted live orders can be printed, shipped and billed.
steps: In live **Settings** > **Integrations** > **API**, select **Show API Key**.
Copy the key as shown. Your client adds live_ for v5.

access: Save the raw key from each dashboard. For v5, send X-API-Key to api.prodigi.com/v5 with sandbox_ or live_ prefixed to the matching key. Sandbox orders stay unbilled, but artwork, saved products and account settings are shared with live. In v4, use the unprefixed key and the matching sandbox or live endpoint.
verify: Read product details or request an order quote in the intended mode. Submit test orders with the sandbox key. Submitting a live order can trigger paid fulfillment.
recover: Check the API version, key and mode. Retrieve or regenerate the key in the corresponding dashboard, then update its Godmode entry and any other consumers.

docs.title: Find API keys and choose sandbox or live mode
